summary: BUG – Mobile Sessions Logging Users Out Automatically
reported_issue: Users on mobile devices are logged out automatically after roughly one hour of inactivity, reported consistently across one customer's team (Haggai Truck Center, 6 users). The reporter could not reproduce it on his own device, suggesting it is isolated to specific accounts/devices/session-handling conditions on mobile.
expected_after_fix: Mobile sessions should not log users out after ~1 hour of inactivity; session/token handling should keep users signed in per the intended session lifetime.
steps_i_followed: Reviewed the reproduction requirements: log in on a mobile device, leave the session idle for ~1 hour, observe automatic logout.
Assessed testability within the automated harness.
actual_now: Not exercised. Reproduction requires (a) ~1 hour of real idle time to trigger the timeout, (b) the specific customer accounts/devices where it occurs (the original reporter could not reproduce it on his own device), and (c) real mobile-device session handling. The verification harness runs in short session windows (staging cookies expire in ~1 hour) and cannot simulate an hour of genuine inactivity nor the account/device-specific conditions, so the auto-logout cannot be observed.
notes: Time-dependent (~1hr inactivity) and account/device-specific session bug. Best verified via backend session/token TTL configuration review and the affected customer's accounts, which are outside this harness. Recommend checking mobile refresh-token / session-cookie TTL and idle-timeout config for the reported accounts.
